title: Deterministic Fingerprint Defect Investigation & Fix

root_cause.summary: Django's connection.cursor(), used for raw SQL, returns jsonb columns as an undecoded str; a bare psycopg2.connect() connection (litrix_db.db()) auto-decodes the same column into a native dict. The str branch of _normalize_scalar() returned such values unmodified/uncanonicalized, while the dict branch already correctly applied json.dumps(sort_keys=True).
root_cause.proof: json.loads(django_str) == raw_dict for both fields, on the real live canary pair; canonical(django) == canonical(raw) after sort_keys=True

scope_bounding.json_like_strings_in_non_jsonb_text_colu: not affected in practice (no such columns exist in FINGERPRINT_RP_FIELDS with this shape); handled safely by the fix regardless
scope_bounding.nested_dicts: affected in principle (same root cause), covered by fix and tests
scope_bounding.lists: affected in principle (same root cause), covered by fix and tests
scope_bounding.null_values: not affected -- identical across both connections
scope_bounding.numeric_values: not affected -- identical across both connections
scope_bounding.boolean_values: not affected -- identical across both connections
scope_bounding.equivalent_key_ordering: was already handled correctly for native dict inputs; the defect was that a str-represented dict never reached that canonicalization path at all

why_previous_checks_did_not_expose_it: all 12 prior live canary confirmations (Phase 4G through the start of Phase 4P) used litrix_db.db() (raw psycopg2), which always takes the already-correct dict branch; Phase 4P's Task D was the first point in the project the fingerprint was computed via Django's connection.cursor(), the actual mechanism execute_approved_merge() is designed to run under

blast_radius.other_canonical_json_serialization_for_m: none found elsewhere in the repository
confirmed_affected_paths: compute_plan_fingerprint() via both real call sites
unaffected_paths: _normalize_authors()'s use of _normalize_scalar() for AuthorNameRaw (always plain text, never jsonb)
merge_approval.py (never computes a fingerprint, only stores/compares opaque string values)

fix.rule: a string is only ever considered for JSON parsing if it structurally looks like a JSON object or array (starts with '{'/'[' and ends with the matching '}'/']', after stripping); parsing failures fall back to plain-string handling without raising; a successful parse into dict/list recurses into the shared dict/list canonicalization branch (json.dumps(sort_keys=True)), which sorts dict keys recursively at every nesting level while never reordering list elements
fix.ordinary_strings_can_be_accidentally_tra: only in the acknowledged, extremely narrow theoretical edge case of a text field that is simultaneously brace/bracket-wrapped edge-to-edge AND syntactically valid JSON -- not realistic for this schema's actual text fields (Title/Abstract/DOI/etc.), and even then the result is deterministic, not incorrect or crash-prone
fix.fix_location: normalization boundary (_normalize_scalar), not adapter-specific hacks in individual callers

regression.delta_reason: 11 new tests added specifically for this defect/fix; zero pre-existing tests modified

compatibility_with_existing_approval.reasoning: the raw psycopg2 path (which produced the stored fingerprint) was already canonical before this fix; the fix makes Django's path converge on that same already-canonical value, not a new one
